_comment_process: pm2 must exec NODE DIRECTLY — never `pnpm worker`, and never the `tsx` CLI.
This config used to be script=pnpm/args=worker, and that is what caused the
46-minute billing outage of 2026-08-29. pm2 tracks the pid it spawns; `pnpm` is a
launcher that exits the instant it is signalled, and the `tsx` CLI spawns yet another
node child. The real worker ran three levels down (pm2 tracked pid 185756, the worker
was 185812), so the shutdown went:
18:34:00.000  pm2 sends SIGINT to pnpm
18:34:00.042  the real worker logs `worker_shutdown` and starts a 25s drain
18:34:00.114  the in-flight billing tick finishes its work
18:34:00.2xx  pnpm exits 0 -> pm2 reads that as 'the app stopped cleanly'
18:34:00.3xx  pm2 treekills 6 pids, taking the still-draining worker with it
The worker was killed between finishing its tick and writing the one statement that
deletes the job and releases its queue lock. graphile-worker expires no queue lock
ever, so `billing_clock` stayed locked by a dead worker until a human ran
force_unlock_workers. Nothing renewed or dunned for 46 minutes while every health
signal read green.
Note that kill_timeout was ALREADY 35000 when this happened. It did not help and could
not: it bounds how long pm2 waits for the pid IT TRACKS, and that pid volunteered to
exit in milliseconds. A drain budget is only real if the process pm2 supervises is the
process doing the draining. That is what this change buys.
`--import tsx` (not the tsx CLI) keeps it to ONE process: tsx registers as an in-process
loader, so pm2's pid is the worker, SIGINT reaches it directly, and kill_timeout finally
governs the real drain. Verified: resolves the `@/` tsconfig alias, single pid.
The engine still runs TypeScript through tsx in production because there is no build
step for it (`pnpm start` is `tsx src/index.ts`). Compiling to dist/ and running plain
node would remove the loader too — worth doing, tracked in docs/PROGRESS.md, and NOT
required for the fix above.
name: tmbilling-worker
_comment_kill_timeout: Must stay STRICTLY GREATER than WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS (25000, src/platform/config.ts).
The worker bounds its own drain at that budget and then exits by itself; pm2's job is
only to not shoot it first. 35000 leaves 10s of headroom for the post-drain work —
closing the health listener, stamping worker_heartbeats, flushing the Cloud Logging
buffer. Lower this below 25000 and you reintroduce the outage above.
_comment_env: PG_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS was a shell default inside the `worker` npm script
(${PG_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS:-60000}). pm2 now execs node directly, so there is no shell
left to expand it and it MUST be set here — dropping it silently unbounds every worker
query, which is the failure mode where one wedged statement looks like a slow tick.
Keep prose OUT of `env`: pm2 ignores unknown keys at the top level, but anything inside
`env` is exported into the process as a real environment variable (verified).
_comment_malloc: MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2: glibc gives each thread its own malloc arena (up to 8 per core) and
keeps what the heavy jobs free there. Measured on production 2026-10-12: 1.9 GB RSS, of
which 1.89 GB anonymous, against a 106 MiB JS heap. Fork mode passes env at spawn, so
it reaches glibc after a reload from this file. The cluster config cannot: deploy/README.md §7.
